newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu to try to reach Arabs in their own tongue.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu to try to reach Arabs in their own tongue.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, having suffered repeated communications breakdowns with Palestinians and the Arab world, wants to spend his spare time learning Arabic on home videocassettes.

"He feels that conversing with and understanding what our Palestinian neighbours say is an advantage," Netanyahu adviser David Bar-Illan told Reuters on Wednesday, saying he would deliver 56 hours of tapes and a guidebook to the right-wing Israeli leader.
Since he came power in June, Netanyahu's hardline declarations - delivered in Hebrew and English - have helped prompt a downward spiral in Israeli-Arab relations.

Ahmad Tibi, adviser to Palestinian President Yasser Arafat, praised Netanyahu's newfound aspiration to communicate with longtime foes but stressed that his hawkish policies would grate Arab ears in any language.
"Language is a good tool of communication," Tibi told Reuters, adding: "I hope that in the future he will manage to have Arab friends."
